acceptance: Freeze a two-executor/one-resource fixture: exactly one live lease may own the resource within a tenant.
Identical operation retries return the original result without extending authority; changed payload under the same operation ID is rejected.
Expiry followed by reacquisition increments the fence; the previous owner cannot renew, release or validate output under the new generation.
Recreate the arbiter over persisted storage and preserve ownership, expiry, generation and idempotency behavior.
Wrong tenant/resource bindings and malformed timestamps, identifiers, TTLs and generations fail closed.
Storage errors never become apparent lease success; concurrent attempts are serialized by the transactional adapter.
Keep current protected HTTP routes unavailable before a real identity/membership verifier is integrated; no caller-selected tenant or forged Access header establishes authority.
Before staging: integrate every effect and artifact sink with current-fence validation and verified grants. Internal lease tests alone do not prove safe distributed execution.
Before hosted admission: prove unknown residency, revoked node, exhausted budget and denied tool cannot trigger fallback execution.
Before launch: interrupt and resume a real repository mission, reject a late old-owner result, restore a hashed checkpoint and produce an exact-head reviewed PR.

Benchmark the same frozen missions, models, budget and review criteria against both manual handoff and an assembled existing coding harness plus persistent cloud workspace plus GitHub PR workflow. Measure reconstruction time, review time, accepted completion and escaped defects; include failed attempts and support in cost.
Before commerce: concurrent reservation, duplicated settlement, cancellation with late usage and refund fixtures pass against existing business contracts.
Before UI release: desktop/mobile/keyboard review binds exact artifacts and distinguishes queued, working, disconnected, waiting-for-approval, failed and complete.
Before recurring pricing: measure repeat use, accepted completion, total supplier cost, review/support time and contribution per accepted mission; unknowns remain unknown.

Proposed pilot expansion gate: at least three of five teams complete at least two accepted missions per week for three consecutive weeks; reconstruction and review time fall without completion-quality degradation versus the assembled baseline; at least two paid renewals occur. These are proposed thresholds, not observed outcomes or authorized prices.
If any proposed pilot threshold is missed, stop breadth expansion and repair the repository mission workflow before adding capability categories or execution providers.
Before promoting this proposal: reconcile SIS #476/#477/#510/#518 and Ops #395/#389 without assuming their open content is accepted architecture.

brief.beneficiary: Technical founders and small product teams operating an existing repository across local coding harnesses and cloud execution.
brief.job: Keep one bounded repository mission coherent while people, harnesses and approved execution machines change.
brief.accepted_outcome: A repository change with exact-source tests, a reviewable PR, artifact lineage and measured usage; an interrupted executor cannot submit an authoritative stale result. This is the target journey, not a claim of hosted availability.
brief.commercial_hypothesis: Keep portable contracts, local operation, reproducible examples and BYOK export in the existing MIT open core. Test a fixed workspace subscription for managed coordination, team controls and recovery, with compute funded separately. Price, margin and willingness to pay remain unapproved and unmeasured. Expand only after the proposed five-team pilot clears its repeat-use, comparative-quality and paid-renewal gates.
brief.first_slice: Implement internal durable fenced lease arbitration at the existing services/starlight-cloud-worker SwarmCoordinator boundary: tenant/resource binding, operation idempotency, acquire/renew/release, generation fencing and restart recovery. Preserve HTTP 503 containment until identity, membership and admission are qualified. Exact implementation and test results belong in the parent release receipt.
brief.next_action: Qualify the internal arbiter with independent review, then integrate verified node identity and current-request admission before an isolated local-to-cloud handoff rehearsal. Compare the same frozen repository missions against manual handoff and an assembled existing coding harness plus persistent cloud workspace plus GitHub PR workflow. After hosted and commercial qualification, test five teams; stop breadth expansion and repair the workflow if the proposed pilot gates are missed. No customer dispatch, pricing or cloud deployment is authorized by this projection.

capabilities.owner: existing source owners and Foundry export adapters

decisions.context: The older Nexus draft mixes catalogue, graph and authority concerns. The current mission product and SIS already own useful boundaries.
options: Existing SIS execution fabric with existing product UI
decisions.choice: Existing SIS execution fabric with existing product UI
decisions.consequences: Nexus names this module. Starlight Intelligence Network describes the federation, without creating another brand, ledger, protocol authority or control plane. This revises draft #476; it is not ratified Registry policy.
decisions.revisit_trigger: A distinct release, audience or permissions boundary is proved and admitted through the Registry.

decisions.context: A disconnected local executor can finish after a replacement starts. In-memory ownership cannot survive isolate eviction.
options: Existing SwarmCoordinator with durable fenced leases
decisions.choice: Existing SwarmCoordinator with durable fenced leases
decisions.consequences: Persist state, operation identity and generation atomically. Gate every artifact-acceptance/effect sink against the current fence; issuing a fence alone cannot prevent stale external writes. Keep protected HTTP contained until verified authority is integrated.
decisions.revisit_trigger: Adversarial race or restart test breaks exclusivity, or measured workload exceeds one-object scope.

decisions.context: A mission can resume on another executor only when its inputs, grants and data boundary permit it.
options: Explicit outbound node pull with checkpoint handoff
decisions.choice: Explicit outbound node pull with checkpoint handoff
decisions.consequences: Use time-bounded leases and source/artifact digests. Transfer explicit task checkpoints, not process memory or entire private machine state. Tunnel is optional connectivity for selected services and never execution authority.
decisions.revisit_trigger: A workload requires interactive inbound service access with a separately reviewed Access policy.

decisions.context: Cloud-oriented executors need immutable private checkpoint bytes. Accepted architecture_media_fabric_v2 still governs web media.
options: Proposed R2 exception for private non-web checkpoints
Existing Vercel Blob for all checkpoint bytes
decisions.choice: Proposed R2 exception for private non-web checkpoints
decisions.consequences: Proposed exception only: non-Vercel execution access and restore are the workload need. SIS owns checkpoint schema; application metadata owns authorization and retention. Admit no new bucket until review, region/retention validation and cost comparison. Start with new checkpoints only; retain legacy references. Roll back adapter selection to owner-local/approved Blob; verify hashes, drain references and remove replicas only after retention obligations. One authoritative object per checkpoint version; optional recovery copies record lineage and expire under policy. No web-media migration.
decisions.revisit_trigger: Measured cost, security or restore evidence fails the chosen adapter, or the Registry declines the exception.

decisions.context: The accepted architecture favors Cloudflare persistent entities and preserves current experience and business owners.
options: Cloudflare durable coordination with existing Vercel/Supabase surfaces
Only local daemon and manual handoff
Assembled coding harness plus persistent cloud workspace plus GitHub PR workflow
decisions.choice: Cloudflare durable coordination with existing Vercel/Supabase surfaces
decisions.consequences: Retain manual/local handoff and compare against an assembled coding harness plus persistent cloud workspace plus GitHub PR workflow on the same frozen tasks, models, budget and review criteria. Evaluate one Sandbox executor after continuity works; snapshot/process limits, isolation and billing must be proven. Preserve one durable workflow owner and existing gateway default; no second wallet.
decisions.revisit_trigger: Held-out missions fail to reduce reconstruction/review time at equal completion quality against the assembled baseline, or the proposed pilot repeat-use/renewal gate is missed. Stop breadth expansion and repair the workflow.

decisions.context: The paid value to test is reliable shared coordination and recovery. Supplier inference and runtime costs vary by mission and must remain attributable.
options: Fixed workspace subscription with separately funded compute
decisions.choice: Fixed workspace subscription with separately funded compute
decisions.consequences: Proposed commercial shape only; no price, checkout change or customer charge is authorized here. Preserve BYOK/self-managed open core. Record supplier cost, failed attempts, review/support and payment fees. Before breadth expansion, require three of five pilot teams to complete two accepted missions weekly for three weeks, reduced reconstruction/review time without completion-quality loss against the assembled baseline, and two paid renewals.
decisions.revisit_trigger: Missed repeat-use, quality, time-saving or renewal threshold; stop expansion and repair the workflow. Unknown contribution margin prevents scaling paid compute.

journey.action: Select an existing repository, outcome, permitted paths, placement and budget.
journey.success: A server-issued scoped mission and reservation exist before work starts.
journey.recovery: Missing identity, grants, balance or residency yields a precise unavailable/denied state.

journey.action: Enroll one approved local node and inspect its declared capabilities.
journey.success: Fresh authenticated evidence identifies the node and allowable tasks.
journey.recovery: Offline, revoked and stale capability reports are visible; no work is sent.

journey.action: Start a bounded change from the laptop.
journey.success: A tenant/resource lease and generation bind the active attempt; progress and source revision are inspectable.
journey.recovery: Retry the same operation identifier only with its unchanged payload.

journey.action: Checkpoint work, disconnect the original executor and resume on an approved target.
journey.success: A new generation is admitted; the target verifies source and checkpoint digests before starting.
journey.recovery: Wait for lease expiry or explicit release. Reject old-owner renewal, completion and artifact promotion.

journey.action: Inspect the PR, evidence and proposed release from desktop or phone.
journey.success: Keyboard/mobile review references the exact artifact hash and head revision.
journey.recovery: Changed output invalidates approval. Loading, disconnected and partial states remain distinct.

journey.action: Accept a useful result or request one bounded revision.
journey.success: One idempotent settlement records actual supplier usage and releases unused allowance.
journey.recovery: Reconcile late usage and uncertain effects; cancellation does not erase incurred cost.

journey.action: Reuse the proven playbook or export the work to another runtime.
journey.success: Repository source, context manifest, event history and artifact references reopen with original provenance.
journey.recovery: Corrupt, missing or unauthorized bytes are rejected. Commercial upgrade stays a hypothesis until repeat use is demonstrated.
